title: Mages of the Dark Medieval
summary: Those born with the Gift to weave spells from the Tapestry, in the year 1230.

claims.text: Only a few are born with or come to the Gift, the knack of weaving spells from the Tapestry of the world; no willpower can grant it.
Whether the Gift is inborn or a grace of angels is argued, but a person either has it fully or not at all.
Mages who use the Gift for others are often remembered later as saints or gods.
In 1230 common superstition supports belief in magic, which helps mages cast with impunity; only in later ages does belief turn against them.

title: Foundations and Pillars
summary: How Dark Ages magic is built.

claims.text: A Pillar is one aspect of a Fellowship's practice, the form its magic takes, and it draws its power from a Foundation.
A Fellowship usually has four Pillars; most mages specialise in one or two.
A new mage starts with Foundation 1 and three dots spread among Pillars.
A spell can do whatever the mage imagines, so long as the mage has enough Pillar and Foundation.

title: Quintessence and Tass
summary: The Fifth Essence, stored and spent to power spells.

claims.text: Quintessence is the raw stuff of the universe, the Fifth Essence behind the other elements.
Mages can hold Quintessence within themselves and spend it on spells.
Tass is Quintessence made solid, in potions, vapours, sacred land or minerals.
Starting Quintessence equals the Cray plus Fount Backgrounds, or 5.

title: Backlash
summary: What befalls a mage whose spell fails badly.

claims.text: A badly failed incantation, summoning or prayer brings Backlash, which almost always harms the caster and often those nearby.
People of the age see Backlash as meddling spirits, divine retribution or one misspoken word of power.
Every point of Quintessence spent on the spell is added to the Backlash.
Branding Backlash leaves marks such as a witch's mark or glassy nails; many small Brandings grow into worse ones.
Manifestation Backlash takes the form of an otherworldly being fitting the caster's tradition, or the local one if far from home.
Dark Ages magic is dynamic within a few fixed frameworks, held by convention rather than nature.
A world-wide consensus reality is still centuries away.

title: The Mystic Fellowships
summary: The magical orders of the Dark Medieval.

claims.text: Most mages, even solitary ones, are heirs to a Fellowship whose world view shapes how they cast and what they think magic is.
Multi-Fellowship cabals are growing less rare in this age.
Fellowships differ in how organised they are; the Hermetics and the Batini are among the most ordered.
Mages drift toward a Fellowship by inclination, unlike vampires who have no say in their clan.

title: Ahl-i-Batin
summary: The Subtle Ones: Muslim philosopher-naturalists seeking the hidden Unity.

claims.text: The Ahl-i-Batin, the Subtle Ones, seek the hidden Unity beneath all things.
They serve their lands as scientists, explorers, diplomats and, when needed, assassins.
They are shunned and distrusted, sometimes even by their own peoples.
Batini tradition claims a history of untold thousands of years, without proof.
Their ranks run Mutasawwif, Murid, Murshid and Qutb.

title: Messianic Voices
summary: Mages of the faith in Christ, who hold the age in their hands.

claims.text: The Messianic Voices began in the Holy Land among Jewish and Greek converts of the Apostles' time.
Once a small part of a larger chorus, their zeal helped win an empire for Christ.
They teach that God grants free will, so a mage chooses to act with God's help, or with the help of angels and saints as conduits.
A healer who asks Saint Luke's aid acts in a way God has ordained, rather than compelling the saint.

title: Order of Hermes
summary: The Hermetic magi, masters of Words.

claims.text: Hermetic magic rises through goetia and theurgia to magia, true magic.
Theurgia teaches a mage to impose will on spirits rather than plead for their favours.
Magia sets aside foci and works through mastery of Words; a rare master may work by will alone.
Hermetics believe no one but themselves practises true magic.
Hermetics scorn other mages, Spirit-Talkers among them, as hedge magicians.

title: The Old Faith
summary: Pagan mages who mourn a more magical world.

claims.text: The Old Faith sees the world as less magical than it once was, and looks back with longing.
Its magic has sunk from forging witch-swords in dragon fire to love potions and fertility charms.
Its many traditions share a respect for the primacy of life, worked through fertility rites and dances.

title: Spirit-Talkers
summary: Mages who bargain with spirits rather than bind them.

claims.text: Spirit-Talkers hold that magic comes from speaking and bargaining with spirits for their knowledge.
They abhor binding a spirit against its will, calling it hubris that threatens the balance between worlds.
Summoning is a central part of their magic.

title: Valdaermen
summary: The Men of Power: mages of the Norse, sworn to Odin.

claims.text: The Valdaermen came with the Vikings and are devoted to Odin, Lord of the Gallows.
Outsiders call their magic dark; to them it is part of their faith.
With Christianity rising and Viking ways fading, they are a dying breed, though still strong.
Even members know their history mostly through oral records and sagas.
